exercise1.prompt: Writing Data Out: Save without the index

hiddenCases.name: the row is written with two fields, so no index came along

exercise1.hint: index=False is the argument that keeps the row numbers out. Reading the first line back is what proves it worked.

exercise2.prompt: Writing Data Out: A round trip that survives
exercise2.hint: to_csv(path, index=False), then pd.read_csv(path), then list(back.columns). Leaving index=False off adds an Unnamed column, which the second check is looking for.

questions.prompt: What does to_csv write by default that you may not want?
choices: The index, as an unnamed first column
questions.explain: Read that file back and you get a column called Unnamed: 0, and it grows every round trip.

questions.prompt: Which argument keeps the row numbers out of the file?
questions.explain: header=False would remove the column names instead, which is almost never what you want.

questions.prompt: When should the index be written out?
choices: When it is meaningful, such as a date or an id
questions.explain: If the index is the label for the row, dropping it loses information; give it a name so the column has a header.

questions.prompt: A saved file has grown Unnamed: 0 and Unnamed: 0.1. What happened?
choices: It has been read and rewritten twice with the index written each time
questions.explain: Each round trip turns the previous index into a real column and then writes a new index beside it.
